items.title: The Spreading Truth
items.question: Textbooks call entropy 'disorder' — teenagers picture messy bedrooms. Physicists increasingly teach it as energy spreading out. What does entropy actually track?
items.correctExplanation: Energy spreading across microstates — disorder metaphors mislead (a tidy crystal can hold more entropy than slush). Spreading, not messiness, is the quantity.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is energy spreading across microstates. Eyes, dishes, and morals miss it: entropy counts energetic arrangements, and tidy ice can outrank messy water. Bedrooms mislead thermodynamics.
items.lessonContent:
Metaphors mislead where quantities clarify.
Spreading, never messiness, is tracked.
Tidy crystals can outrank slushy melts.
Bedrooms are terrible thermodynamic models.
Share this: retire one disorder metaphor.

items.title: The Open Kitchen
items.question: Creationists argue evolution violates the second law (order from chaos). Earth, however, bathes in solar influx while radiating waste heat. Why is there no violation?
choices: The second law applies only to isolated systems
items.correctAnswer: The second law applies only to isolated systems
items.correctExplanation: Only isolated systems — Earth trades energy with space: low-entropy sunlight in, high-entropy heat out. Local order paid by solar income.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the second law applies only to isolated systems. Law-breaking, pauses, and exemptions miss it: open systems order themselves on through-flows. Life is a solar-powered eddy, fully lawful.
items.lessonContent:
Open systems order on through-flows lawfully.
Isolation scopes the second law strictly.
Solar income funds biological complexity.
Eddies obey rivers they ride within.
Share this: audit one open system.

items.title: The Costly Meal
items.question: Schrödinger said life feeds on 'negative entropy' — importing order to stave off decay. Every meal, at bottom, imports what?
items.correctExplanation: Low-entropy arrangement — food's value is structural order organisms dismantle for work. Calories count energy; arrangement counts usefulness.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is low-entropy arrangement. Heat, morals, and water miss it: bodies harvest molecular order, excreting disorder as heat and waste. Eating is entropy arbitrage.
items.lessonContent:
Bodies harvest order, excrete disorder.
Arrangement counts beyond calories.
Entropy arbitrage funds all living.
Order imported staves decay daily.
Share this: eat one negentropy lunch.

items.title: The Final Equilibrium
items.question: Cosmology's heat death pictures a universe expanded into uniform lukewarm equilibrium. What ends when gradients vanish?
items.correctExplanation: All change, work, and life — gradients drive everything; equilibrium drives nothing. The end is boredom, not bang.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is all change, work, and life. Matter persists, gravity holds, time flows — but nothing happens anywhere. Difference, not substance, is existence's fuel.
items.lessonContent:
Gradients drive; equilibrium idles forever.
Difference fuels existence, not substance.
Boredom, not bang, ends universes.
Work needs slopes of every kind.
Share this: cherish one gradient today.

items.title: The Unrecyclable Remainder
items.question: Enthusiasts promise fully circular economies, but thermodynamics mandates losses: dissipation, mixing, contamination. What can recycling never fully defeat?
items.correctExplanation: Entropy's toll — every cycle scatters some material beyond economic recovery. Circularity approaches but never arrives.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is entropy's dissipative toll. Greed, laziness, and bins miss it: physics taxes each loop with dispersion. Perfect circles violate the second law's economics.
items.lessonContent:
Physics taxes every loop with losses.
Dispersion defeats perfect circularity.
Approach circles; never promise them.
Tolls apply regardless of virtue.
Share this: trace one dissipative loss.

items.title: The Energy Ledger
items.question: Energy Return on Investment divides energy delivered by energy spent getting it. Early oil returned ~100:1; modern sources return far less. What does falling EROI mean?
choices: More effort per unit of useful energy
items.correctAnswer: More effort per unit of useful energy
items.correctExplanation: More effort per useful unit — civilization runs on surplus energy, and shrinking surpluses squeeze everything built atop them. Net energy, not gross, powers societies.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is more effort per unit of useful energy. Profits, chemistry, and sunlight miss it: EROI measures physical surplus before economics. Societies spend net, never gross.
items.lessonContent:
Net energy powers societies, never gross.
Surpluses squeezed strain everything atop.
Physical returns precede economic ones.
Ledger energy before pricing it.
Share this: compute one EROI roughly.

items.title: The Coal Paradox
items.question: Efficient steam engines were meant to save coal; coal use soared instead, as cheaper power multiplied uses. What paradox is this?
items.correctExplanation: Efficiency raising total consumption — Jevons paradox: cheaper steam expanded applications faster than savings accumulated. Frugality per unit, profligacy in total.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is efficiency raising total consumption. Breakdowns, celebrations, and discoveries miss it: falling costs grow demand beyond engineering savings. Economies rebound past engineers' arithmetic.
items.lessonContent:
Falling costs grow demand past savings.
Frugality per unit, profligacy in total.
Rebounds outrun engineering arithmetic.
Efficiency needs caps to save anything.
Share this: spot one Jevons rebound.

items.title: The Driven Miles
items.question: Fuel-efficient cars get driven extra miles, clawing back part of the engineering savings. What is this take-back called?
items.correctExplanation: Direct rebound — cheaper miles invite more miles: 10-30% of savings typically return as driving. Efficiency leaks through behavior.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is direct rebound effect. Failures, tires, and taxes miss it: per-mile savings fund extra miles directly. Engineering gains share proceeds with behavior.
items.lessonContent:
Per-mile savings fund extra miles.
Behavior shares engineering proceeds.
Take-backs run ten to thirty percent.
Efficiency leaks through use patterns.
Share this: track one rebound of yours.

items.title: The Finite Pie
items.question: Ecological economists argue endless GDP growth on a finite planet collides with material-energy realities. What ultimately constrains perpetual growth?
items.correctExplanation: Material-energy throughput limits — economies metabolize matter and energy; planets supply finite flows. Growth hits physics before imagination.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is material-energy throughput limits. Bankers, ads, and bandwidth miss it: throughput, not money, binds. Dematerialization helps at margins; physics holds the totals.
items.lessonContent:
Throughput binds where money only measures.
Metabolisms need material flows always.
Margins yield; totals obey physics.
Growth meets geology eventually.
Share this: weigh one throughput limit.

items.title: The Exported Smoke
items.question: Factories vent smoke freely while neighbors cough: real costs dumped outside market prices. Economically, what is pollution?
items.correctExplanation: An unpriced entropy export — disorder shipped off-book to shared airs and waters. Prices lie by omission; lungs keep true ledgers.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is an unpriced entropy export. Gifts, strategies, and errors miss it: externalities are thermodynamic dumping with the invoice torn up. Markets optimize the priced and ignore the rest.
items.lessonContent:
Invoices torn up don't cancel costs.
Lungs keep ledgers markets omit.
Disorder shipped off-book returns as harm.
Prices lie most by omission.
Share this: price one externality.

items.title: The Thinning Vein
items.question: Copper ores slid from ~4% metal to under 1%; each ton now demands far more energy and rock moved. What makes modern mining hungrier?
items.correctExplanation: Declining ore grades — rich veins mined first leave lean rock: energy per ton climbs as concentration falls. Geology grades on a curve downward.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is declining ore grades. Laziness, helmets, and lunches miss it: concentration dictates energy cost directly. First fruits were richest; tailings grow leaner.
items.lessonContent:
Concentration dictates energy cost directly.
First fruits run richest always.
Lean rock demands fat energy.
Grades slide; costs climb correspondingly.
Share this: trace one thinning vein.

items.title: The Flow Peak
items.question: 'Peak oil' was misread as running dry; the real crunch is flow rates — how fast wells deliver, not totals underground. What actually peaks?
items.correctExplanation: Extractable flow rate — economies burn flows, not stocks: delivery speed constrains before reserves empty. Peaks are about pace.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is extractable flow rate. Prices, volumes, and careers miss it: civilization drinks from a straw, and straws narrow first. Stocks comfort; flows command.
items.lessonContent:
Straws narrow before wells empty.
Flows command where stocks comfort.
Delivery speed constrains economies first.
Pace peaks precede volume peaks.
Share this: watch one flow narrow.

items.title: The Hundred Millennia
items.question: Some nuclear waste stays dangerous 100,000+ years — longer than writing, cities, or states have existed. What unprecedented problem is this?
items.correctExplanation: Deep-time stewardship — guarding hazards across civilizational timescales no institution has survived. Waste outlives every warden imagined.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is deep-time stewardship. Costs, paint, and flavors miss it: the problem is temporal, not technical — warning beings 3,000 generations hence. Ethics must outlive languages.
items.lessonContent:
Hazards outlive every imagined warden.
Temporal problems dwarf technical ones.
Warnings must cross civilizational gaps.
Stewardship spans a hundred millennia.
Share this: warn one distant descendant.

items.title: The Discounted Future
items.question: Climate economics hinges on discounting: Stern's near-zero pure time preference versus Nordhaus's higher rate moves trillions. What is truly debated?
items.correctExplanation: Discounting future welfare — how much less tomorrow's lives count is ethics disguised as math. Rates are moral philosophy with decimal points.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is discounting future welfare ethically. Brands, forecasts, and dating miss it: pure time preference prices unborn lives. Trillions swing on moral parameters.
items.lessonContent:
Rates are moral philosophy decimalized.
Decimals price unborn lives directly.
Trillions hinge on ethical parameters.
Math disguises morals here completely.
Share this: price one future life.

items.title: The Carbon Purse
items.question: For 1.5°C, humanity may emit only ~400 GtCO₂ more — a finite stock, not a yearly rate that resets. What does the budget frame?
items.correctExplanation: A finite total stock — every ton spends shared purse permanently. Budgets make procrastination visible as spending.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a finite total stock. Variance, bills, and cycles miss it: stocks don't reset January first. Delay spends; the purse notices.
items.lessonContent:
Stocks never reset January first.
Delay spends from shared purses.
Procrastination is visible spending here.
Purses notice what calendars forgive.
Share this: spend one carbon ton mindfully.

items.title: The One-Way Door
items.question: Ice sheets and rainforests may flip past thresholds with no return trip at any price — collapse now, regret forever. What makes these special?
items.correctExplanation: Irreversible thresholds — one-way doors in Earth systems: crossing costs everything, uncrossing costs impossibility. Precaution prices asymmetry.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is irreversible thresholds. Reversibility, cheapness, and fame miss it: some doors lock behind crossers permanently. Asymmetry demands precaution mathematics.
items.lessonContent:
Doors lock behind crossers permanently.
Asymmetry demands precaution math.
Crossing costs everything; return costs impossibility.
One-way systems punish experiments.
Share this: respect one locked door.

items.title: The Costly Kilogram
items.question: Roughly 10% of energy passes each trophic level — a beef kilogram costs many feed kilograms. What does this rule imply for diets?
items.correctExplanation: Meat's thermodynamic costliness — each level taxes 90%: eat low for energetic thrift. Trophic arithmetic favors plants enormously.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is meat's thermodynamic costliness. Taste, labor, and photosynthesis miss it: tenths compound cruelly up food chains. Diets are energy strategies wearing culture.
items.lessonContent:
Tenths compound cruelly up chains.
Low eating is energetic thrift.
Diets strategize energy under culture.
Plants win thermodynamic accounting.
Share this: eat one level lower.

items.title: The Pale Harvest
items.question: Crops convert barely 1-2% of sunlight to biomass — reflection, off-spectrum light, and respiration claim the rest. Why is harvest so thin?
items.correctExplanation: Losses at every step — reflection, spectrum mismatch, photorespiration, maintenance: physics taxes photons repeatedly. Thin harvests are honest accounting.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is losses at every conversion step. Laziness, scarcity, and plots miss it: each transformation keeps its cut. Biomass is what survives the gauntlet.
items.lessonContent:
Gauntlets tax photons repeatedly.
Thin harvests are honest accounting.
Each transformation keeps its cut.
Biomass survives stacked losses.
Share this: thank one surviving photon.

items.title: The Mandatory Waste
items.question: No heat engine beats the Carnot limit fixed by reservoir temperatures. Waste heat isn't poor engineering but what?
items.correctExplanation: Thermodynamic necessity — temperature gaps cap conversion absolutely: some heat must exit. Necessity, not negligence, warms rivers.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is thermodynamic necessity. Unions, materials, and luck miss it: the second law takes its cut from every engine. Perfect conversion is forbidden, not merely difficult.
items.lessonContent:
Second law takes cuts from all engines.
Forbidden differs from difficult entirely.
Necessity warms rivers, not negligence.
Gaps cap conversions absolutely.
Share this: forgive one warm river.

items.title: The Impossible Efficiency
items.question: Heat pumps deliver 3-4 heat units per electricity unit — over 100% 'efficient' without breaking physics. How is this possible?
choices: Moving ambient heat, not making it
items.correctAnswer: Moving ambient heat, not making it
items.correctExplanation: Moving, not making — pumps relocate ambient warmth instead of manufacturing it. Efficiency exceeds 100% because the denominator counts only the moving work.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is moving ambient heat, not making it. Perpetual motion, faulty meters, and secret fuel miss it: relocation beats creation thermodynamically. Pump, don't produce.
items.lessonContent:
Relocation beats creation thermodynamically.
Denominators count moving work only.
Pump ambient; don't manufacture.
Over-100% is bookkeeping, not magic.
Share this: move one unit of warmth.

items.title: The Erasure Price
items.question: Erasing one bit of information costs at least kT ln 2 of energy — computation has a thermodynamic floor. What sets this minimum?
items.correctExplanation: Landauer's limit — forgetting is physical: erased bits heat the universe measurably. Information is thermodynamic currency.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is Landauer's limit. Moore, Metcalfe, and Murphy miss it: erasure dissipates, reversibility excepted. Forgetting costs; computers pay in heat.
items.lessonContent:
Forgetting costs physical currency.
Erased bits heat universes measurably.
Information is thermodynamic throughout.
Floors exist beneath all computing.
Share this: erase one bit reverently.

items.title: The Demon's Ledger
items.question: Maxwell's demon sorts molecules seemingly for free — until physicists billed the measurement itself. What exorcises the demon?
items.correctExplanation: Information's physical cost — knowing which molecule goes where costs entropy that pays the books. Demons starve on honest accounting.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is information has physical cost. Bigger, faster, and larger miss it: measurement and memory are thermodynamic acts. Ledgers balance; demons default.
items.lessonContent:
Knowing costs entropy always.
Measurement is thermodynamic action.
Ledgers balance; demons default.
Honest accounting starves paradoxes.
Share this: price one measurement.

items.title: The Stubborn Sectors
items.question: Aviation, steel, and cement resist electrification — energy density, blast heat, and process chemistry block easy swaps. What makes them hardest?
items.correctExplanation: No easy substitutes — physics, not will, blocks: batteries can't fly far, furnaces need carbon chemistry. Hard sectors need new processes, not pep talks.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is no easy physical substitutes. Unions, effort, and PR miss it: constraints are material. Decarbonizing atoms differs from decarbonizing electrons.
items.lessonContent:
Material constraints beat pep talks.
Atoms decarbonize harder than electrons.
Substitutes missing means processes needed.
Physics, not will, blocks hardest.
Share this: respect one hard sector.

items.title: The Mile Myth
items.question: Food miles dominate green-eating debates, yet production method dwarfs transport in most footprints. What matters more than distance traveled?
items.correctExplanation: How it was grown — production dominates footprints: heated greenhouses out-emit field imports. Methods outweigh mileage massively.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is how it was grown. Colors, brands, and shelves miss it: analyses rank production first, transport a distant second. Miles mislead; methods matter.
items.lessonContent:
Production dominates footprints decisively.
Methods outweigh mileage massively.
Greenhouses out-emit imports routinely.
Miles mislead; methods matter.
Share this: grow one awareness.

items.title: The Limestone Debt
items.question: Cement emits CO₂ not just from kiln fuel but from limestone's own chemistry (calcination). Why do these emissions resist fixes?
items.correctExplanation: Chemistry itself releases it — CaCO₃ becomes CaO plus CO₂ by formula, not by fuel choice. Process emissions ignore energy swaps.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is chemistry itself releases CO₂. Workers, paint, and bags miss it: the reaction exhales regardless of heat source. Formulas, not furnaces, set the floor.
items.lessonContent:
Formulas set floors furnaces cannot.
Reactions exhale regardless of fuel.
Process emissions ignore energy swaps.
Chemistry constrains before engineering.
Share this: read one formula's exhaust.
